claims.text: The driver is the filing party here, and the disputed money is already off the rider: EV-FARE-06057 records payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00, and EV-TRIP-06057 carries the interim reversal at 2026-09-29T08:13:10 (5.00 SGD refunded to the rider and withheld from the driver pending review). Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands; the outcome is party-relative and never means 'restore a charge'. The driver, having chosen to file, must therefore make out every element of a valid no-show on this record before the already-issued refund can be undone.

The rider does not contest the contact element of POL-NS-23 and will not ask the judge to read a defect into a record where there is none: the driver sent two in-app chat messages (EV-CHAT-06057, MSG-06057-001 at 06:47:00 and MSG-06057-002 at 06:51:10) and placed two in-app calls (EV-TRIP-06057 in_app_calls, 06:53:20 for 25 s and 06:56:00 for 20 s, neither answered), all before the 06:58:10 cancellation, so on the face of the clause the contact obligation is met. The rider's case is not built on denying that.

The rider likewise does not contest the timing element of POL-NS-21: the free wait runs from the scheduled pickup time (06:50:00) to 06:55:00, and the driver cancelled at 06:58:10, 190 s after it, so the wait was served and the rider does not argue otherwise. The rider notes only that the platform ran its own timer from the driver's early arrival (wait_timer_started 06:46:35, wait_timer_expired 06:51:35) and expired it 3 min 25 s before the policy's free wait ended, so the process the driver was working to on the night was not POL-NS-21's clock.

claims.text: The no-show cancellation was made after the free wait expired. The driver arrived at 06:46:30, before the 06:50 scheduled pickup, so under POL-NS-21 the free wait of 300 s runs from scheduled_at (06:50) and ends at 06:55; the trip record shows the driver did not cancel until 06:58:10, i.e. 490 s after the free-wait clock started. Every condition POL-NS-21 sets for cancelling as a rider no-show was therefore satisfied.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is fully met, so the FULL_REFUND that clause licenses is not available on this record. The chat log shows two in-app messages sent by the driver at 06:47:00 and 06:51:10 (both delivered and read), and the trip record shows two in-app calls placed by the driver at 06:53:20 (rang 25 s) and 06:56:00 (rang 20 s) - both chat and call contact occurred before the 06:58:10 cancellation, which is exactly the conjunction POL-NS-23 requires.

The driver was not late, so the rider's free-cancellation right under POL-NS-24 never arose and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due. The scheduled pickup was 06:50 and the deadline POL-NS-24 fixes is the scheduled time plus 5 minutes, i.e. 06:55:00; the driver arrived at 06:46:30, well inside that deadline, and the derived arrival check records arrived_by_deadline as true.

The GPS trace independently corroborates the arrival the trip record asserts, so the arrival fact does not rest on the platform record alone. The driver-device trace carries 47 fixes at 30 s intervals with 100% coverage, no gap above 30 s and a reported accuracy on every fix (max 9 m); the nearest fix to the pickup point is 3.59 m away with a 4 m accuracy, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and the trace then holds at zero speed from 06:46:30 through 06:58:00 - the vehicle was physically standing at the pickup for the whole wait.

The fee the platform charged matches the policy fee exactly, so there is no fee-amount defect for the rider to exploit. The payments ledger records a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD, reconciles to a total_charged of 5.00 SGD, and carries fee_matches_policy as true against the 5.00 SGD no-show fee with a 1.00 share to the driver that POL-NS-22 prescribes.

The interim reversal now standing on the ledger is the very thing the driver is contesting, and NO_ACTION would leave it standing against him. The fare breakdown shows payment_status REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.0 and a fee_reversed event at 08:13:10 reversing the 5.00 SGD to the rider and withholding it from the driver; because the driver filed and the charge has already been moved, NO_ACTION is a loss for the driver under POL-GEN-03's party-relative reading. Since POL-NS-22 provides the fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, the ruling must be DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The rider's counter-account does not survive the timestamps. The rider says the driver 'cancelled on me only a few minutes after the booking time', but on the record the cancellation came 8 minutes 10 seconds after the 06:50 scheduled pickup, and 11 minutes 40 seconds after the driver first stood at the pickup at 06:46:30; the rider was notified the driver had arrived at 06:46:34 and read the driver's first message at 06:47:18, and the free wait ran its full course to 06:55 and beyond without the rider boarding. The driver's account of waiting, messaging and calling is the one the contemporaneous record supports.

There is no open question here that would force an escalation under POL-GEN-26. The traffic advisory artifact is absent - EV-ADVIS-06057-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it carries no fact in either direction - but no rule that governs this no-show depends on traffic data: arrival, the length of the wait, and pre-cancellation contact are each carried by artifacts that are COMPLETE at weight 1.0. POL-GEN-02(3) gives the absent artifact no weight, so its absence cannot manufacture an unestablished fact, and the driver's early arrival means no traffic excuse was ever needed.

The procedural posture confirms the fee can and should be restored by the AI. Neither party's profile carries a fraud flag (rider and driver fraud_flags both 0), so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence bar is not engaged, and the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; POL-NS-26 makes the ruling on a no-show final on the same footing.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties agree on the operative facts, and the contemporaneous record decides the case.

To the driver: your no-show charge on TRP-06057 was validly incurred, and the 5.00 SGD that the platform refunded to the rider and withheld from you on 2026-09-29 at 08:13:10 (EV-TRIP-06057, fee_reversed; EV-FARE-06057, payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00) is to be returned to you. You arrived at the pickup at 06:46:30, before the 06:50 scheduled pickup (EV-TRIP-06057, arrived_at). Under POL-NS-21, where the driver arrives before the scheduled time the 300 s free wait runs from the scheduled time, so it ran from 06:50 to 06:55; you cancelled at 06:58:10, 190 seconds after it expired (derived free_wait.cancelled_after_free_wait true). You also met POL-NS-23: two in-app chat messages at 06:47:00 and 06:51:10 (EV-CHAT-06057, both delivered and read) and two in-app calls at 06:53:20 and 06:56:00 (EV-TRIP-06057, in_app_calls), all before the cancellation. The fee charged was exactly the policy figure of 5.00 SGD and the ledger reconciles to total_charged 5.00 SGD with fee_matches_policy true (EV-FARE-06057), so POL-NS-22's fee-amount referral does not fire and the ruling acts on the 5.00 SGD that stands. Because you were not late - you arrived well inside the 06:55 deadline (derived driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline true) - POL-NS-24 gives the rider no free-cancellation right and no goodwill credit is due.

To the rider: your own advocate conceded the contact element (POL-NS-23) and the timing element (POL-NS-21), so nothing in your account resists the driver's case on the merits. Your point that the platform ran its app timer from the driver's early arrival and expired it at 06:51:35, before the policy's free wait ended at 06:55, is correct as a fact (EV-TRIP-06057, wait_timer_started 06:46:35, wait_timer_expired 06:51:35) but it does not assist you: the driver waited past the policy's free wait regardless, and POL-NS-21 measures the wait from the scheduled time, not from the app's clock. The driver filed this case, and the money is currently off the rider and out of the driver's hands; because the no-show was valid, the present state is not what the record supports, and the 5.00 SGD is returned to the driver. That is the DRIVER_COMPENSATION figure of 5.00 SGD carried in both amount fields, being the money the ruling moves.

Confidence: the facts that decide this case - arrival, the length of the wait, and pre-cancellation contact - are carried by EV-TRIP-06057, EV-GPS-06057 (driver-device trace, 100% coverage, nearest fix 3.59 m from the pickup against a 4 m reported accuracy, holding at zero speed from 06:46:30 to 06:58:00) and EV-CHAT-06057, each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, corroborated by the rider's own concessions. The absent traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06057-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact (POL-GEN-02(3)); no rule here turns on traffic data, and the driver's early arrival means no traffic excuse was ever needed, so POL-GEN-26 raises no open question. The dispute value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, and both profiles show fraud_flags 0 (EV-RPROF-06057, EV-DPROF-06057), so POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final at any confidence; the confidence stated is 0.95, within the 1.0 cap the complete artifacts set. No referral arises: the fee equals the policy 5.00 SGD (POL-NS-22), the driver was not late (POL-NS-24), and the rider profile carries no no_show_cancellations_30d counter for POL-NS-25.

To Driver D-87885 and Rider R-80095: this is the ruling on the 5.00 SGD no-show cancellation fee for trip TRP-06057. The no-show was valid, the fee stands, and because the platform had already refunded the 5.00 SGD to the rider and recovered it from the driver, the driver is owed that 5.00 SGD back. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, and under POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carry that same 5.00 SGD.

Why the fee stands. (1) Arrival and wait, POL-NS-21: the scheduled pickup was 06:50:00; the driver arrived at 06:46:30, before the scheduled time, so the 300 s free wait ran from scheduled_at and ended at 06:55:00; the driver did not cancel until 06:58:10, i.e. 190 s after the free wait expired and 490 s after the clock started. The driver-device GPS trace (EV-GPS-06057: 47 fixes, 100% coverage, no gap over 30 s, every fix reporting accuracy, max 9 m) shows the vehicle stationary at the pickup from 06:46:30 through 06:58:00, nearest fix 3.59 m away with 4 m accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius. (2) Contact, POL-NS-23: the driver sent two in-app messages (EV-CHAT-06057, 06:47:00 and 06:51:10) and placed two in-app calls (EV-TRIP-06057, 06:53:20 for 25 s and 06:56:00 for 20 s, neither answered), all before the 06:58:10 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met and the FULL_REFUND that clause licenses does not arise; the rider expressly did not contest this. (3) Timeliness, POL-NS-24: the deadline was scheduled time plus 5 minutes, 06:55:00, and the driver arrived at 06:46:30, well inside it, so no free-cancellation right arose and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit is due. (4) The fee, POL-NS-22: the payments ledger (EV-FARE-06057) carries a single cancellation-fee line of 5.00 SGD reconciling to a total_charged of 5.00 SGD, exactly the policy fee, so there is no fee-amount defect and no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral.

The rider's points. The rider did not contest the timing or contact elements. The rider's counter-account ('he came early and then cancelled on me only a few minutes after the booking time') is not borne out: the driver was at the pickup from 06:46:30 and cancelled 11 minutes 40 seconds later, 8 minutes 10 seconds after the 06:50:00 booking time. The rider's observation that the platform's own timer expired at 06:51:35 is noted, but that is the platform's process clock, not POL-NS-21's free-wait clock; the cancellation at 06:58:10 is after the policy free wait on any reading.

The filing frame. The driver filed and the disputed 5.00 SGD has already been moved to the rider and withheld from the driver (fee_reversed at 2026-09-29T08:13:10+08:00; EV-FARE-06057 payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.00). Since the fare rules give the fee to the driver as compensation and the driver has made out every element, the driver is the party owed the money, so per POL-GEN-03 the outcome is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD rather than NO_ACTION.

No referrals. POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire because the driver arrived on time and attempted contact; POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not fire because exactly 5.00 SGD was charged; and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show counter (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d) is not present on this rider's profile, so no review flag is added. The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06057-01, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) establishes nothing, and no rule governing this no-show turns on traffic data, so POL-GEN-26 does not escalate the case.

Confidence. The deciding facts are carried by complete artifacts at weight 1.0 (EV-TRIP-06057, EV-GPS-06057, EV-CHAT-06057, EV-FARE-06057), all COMPLETE with no issue codes. The contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag, so the AI ruling is final (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26). Confidence 0.95.

Arrival and the wait (POL-NS-21). The driver arrived at 06:46:30 (EV-TRIP-06057), before the 06:50 scheduled pickup, so the 300-second free wait ran from the scheduled time: 06:50 to 06:55. He did not cancel until 06:58:10, 490 seconds after the wait clock started and after it expired. The fee (POL-NS-22). The ledger charged exactly 5.00 SGD, matching the policy no-show fee, so there is no fee-amount defect and no referral under POL-NS-22 arises; that clause provides the fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

The rider's two points are accepted but do not change the outcome. The rider is right that the driver, as filer, bears the burden of making out every element of a valid no-show before the already-issued refund can be undone (POL-GEN-03, party-relative); he has discharged it. Timing (POL-NS-21): the trip was scheduled for 06:50 and the driver arrived at 06:46:30, before the schedule, so the 300 s free wait ran from 06:50:00 to 06:55:00. The driver did not cancel until 06:58:10, 190 s after the free wait ended. The rider's advocate does not contest this, and it is right not to: the platform's own timer (started 06:46:35, expired 06:51:35) is not the policy clock.

The nearest fix is 3.59 m from the pickup with 4 m accuracy, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, and the trace holds at zero speed from 06:46:30 through 06:58:00.

Contact (POL-NS-23): the driver sent two in-app messages (06:47:00 and 06:51:10) and placed two in-app calls (06:53:20 and 06:56:00), all before the 06:58:10 cancellation - the conjunction the clause requires. The rider's advocate concedes this element.

Late arrival (POL-NS-24): the driver arrived well before the 06:55 deadline, so no free-cancellation right and no 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arise, and no referral on this clause fires.

Fee (POL-NS-22): the fee charged was exactly 5.00 SGD, matching the policy fee, so no fee-amount referral fires; with every element of the no-show met, POL-NS-22 gives the fee to the driver as compensation for time and fuel.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06057-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact, and no rule governing this no-show needs traffic data, so it neither creates an open question under POL-GEN-26 nor caps confidence. The rider's position - that under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling would leave the refund standing - is a correct description of the present state, but the present state cannot stand once every element of the no-show is established. Because the driver filed and is owed the whole 5.00 SGD that was refunded to the rider and recovered from him, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carrying that 5.00 SGD figure.
